name: PCA82C251T_YM,118
title: CAN transceiver for 24 V systems
summary: A single-channel high-speed CAN transceiver that links a CAN protocol controller to a two-wire differential bus, built for ISO 11898-24 V truck and bus networks up to 1 MBd. Its bus pins withstand −36 V to +36 V and survive shorts to a 24 V battery or to ground; the driver is current limited, and the limit drops when the junction runs hot. One pin, Rs, picks high-speed, slope-controlled or low-current standby operation.

circuits.title: CAN node with a P8xC592 controller
circuits.description: The transceiver between a P8xC592 microcontroller's CAN port and the bus. CTX0 drives TXD, RXD returns to CRX0, and Vref goes to the controller's CRX1 input. Port pin PX,Y reaches Rs through Rext; a HIGH on Rs selects standby. VCC is a +5 V rail with 100 nF to ground. CANH and CANL run to the bus line, which carries two 120 Ω resistors across it.

parts.note: slope resistor; 0 Ω without slope control

notes: The P8xC592 output control register is set to 1AH: push-pull outputs, dominant = LOW.
With no slope control wanted, Rext = 0.

circuits.title: Dynamic characteristics test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit the timing figures are measured in. VCC is +5 V with 100 nF to ground. The bus is loaded by 60 Ω in parallel with 100 pF between CANH and CANL, RXD carries 30 pF to ground, and Rext runs from Rs to ground. TXD is the driven input; Vref and RXD are the observed outputs.

circuits.title: Automotive transient test circuit
circuits.description: The circuit the bus-pin transient rating is tested in. VCC is +5 V with 100 nF to ground and Rs goes to ground through 47 kΩ. CANH and CANL are loaded by 60 Ω between them, and each line is coupled through its own 500 pF capacitor to one Schaffner generator output. The generator applies the ISO 7637 part 1 pulses 1, 2, 3a and 3b.

where.Rth(vj-a): thermal resistance, virtual junction to ambient; Rth(j-a) is 160 K/W typ in free air

operation.text: The part turns the CAN controller's logic-level TXD into a differential drive on CANH and CANL, and turns the bus's differential level back into logic on RXD. It is aimed at trucks and buses running ISO 11898-24 V at up to 1 MBd, and a bus can hold at least 110 nodes.

TXD LOW drives CANH HIGH and CANL LOW: a dominant bit, RXD 0. TXD HIGH or open lets both lines float: recessive, RXD 1 unless another node is driving dominant. In standby (VRs > 0.75VCC) and whenever VCC is below 4.5 V the bus lines float, so an unpowered node leaves the bus undisturbed.

A current limit on the transmitter output stage keeps it intact through a short of either bus line to the positive or negative battery; dissipation is higher for as long as the short lasts. Short-circuit CANH current is 200 mA max (magnitude) at V7 = −5 V, and CANL 200 mA max at V6 = 36 V.

Near 160 °C junction temperature both transmitter outputs fall back to a lower current limit. The transmitter dissipates most of the chip's power, so the die cools; the receiver and the rest of the IC stay in operation. Bus-line shorts are the case this covers.
CANH and CANL are protected against the electrical transients of a vehicle supply; the rating is −200 V to +200 V, tested with ISO 7637 part 1 pulses 1, 2, 3a and 3b.

Pin 8 sets one of three modes. High-speed: Rs below 0.3VCC, normally tied to ground; the driver switches as fast as it can with no edge shaping, and a shielded cable is advised against RFI. Slope control: a resistor from Rs to ground draws 10 µA to 200 µA, the pin sits at 0.4VCC to 0.6VCC, and the edge rate follows that current, which allows unshielded twisted or parallel wire; with 47 kΩ the slew rate is 7 V/µs typ. Standby: Rs above 0.75VCC.

In standby the driver is off and the receiver runs at reduced current (275 µA max supply). A dominant level on the bus (differential voltage above 0.9 V) still pulls RXD LOW within 3 µs; the controller answers by bringing Rs low to return to normal operation, which takes up to 20 µs. The standby receiver is slow, so at higher bit rates the first message is lost.

RXD goes LOW once the differential input passes 0.9 V and returns HIGH once it falls below 0.5 V, with 150 mV typ hysteresis between the two switching points. Timing is measured from TXD's edge to Vdiff reaching 0.9 V (bus active) or 0.5 V (bus inactive), and to RXD crossing 0.3VCC or 0.7VCC.
Vref sits at mid-supply: 0.45VCC to 0.55VCC with Rs at 1 V and up to 50 µA load, widening to 0.4VCC to 0.6VCC with Rs at 4 V and up to 5 µA.
The highest reflow peak temperature follows J-STD-020C, set by the package's thickness and its volume. The moisture sensitivity precautions marked on the packing apply.
